title: Bounded constructibility of every finite-type direct image
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between finite-type schemes over
a field $k$, and let $A$ be a finite ring annihilated by an
integer invertible in $k$. Then

$$
Rf_*:D^b_c(X,A)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,A)
$$

is defined on the ordinary derived categories. The morphism
$f$ need not be separated.
The notation refers to bounded constructible complexes.

proof.text: Fix $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$. A finite-type $k$-scheme has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] each such spectrum is Noetherian. A descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes on each member of a finite cover, hence globally. Consequently $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian and every open is quasi-compact: otherwise successively adjoining opens to a union with no finite subcover produces a strictly increasing chain of opens. Every open of either scheme is again of finite type over $k$: cover it by finitely many distinguished affine opens in the original affine charts, whose coordinate rings are finitely generated algebras localized at one element.

source.place: Paragraph 1: finite affine covers and quasi-compact intersections

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below complex $J^\bullet$ of injective $A_X$-module sheaves representing $K$, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Open restriction is exact: kernels are sectionwise and a local lift of a cokernel section remains a local lift on the localized site. It preserves zero maps. For an open $U$, [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-adjunction] supplies an additive left adjoint $G$ to restriction preserving finite limits and colimits, hence exact. For a monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow N$ on $U$, a map $M\to J^q|_U$ corresponds to $G(M)\to J^q$, which extends across $G(M)\hookrightarrow G(N)$; adjunction gives the desired extension. Thus $J|_U$ is still bounded below and termwise injective, and represents $K|_U$. It computes every derived direct image of this restriction by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and clause (2) of the injective-representative lemma.

source.place: Paragraphs 1–2: choose the injective representative and restrict it to opens

proof.text: For an open $V\subseteq Y$, put $X_V=f^{-1}(V)$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$. On an etale $W\to V$, both $(f_*J)|_V$ and $(f_V)_*(J|_{X_V})$ have value $J(W\times_Y X)$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The identification respects the resolution differential, so step 2 identifies $(Rf_*K)|_V$ with $R(f_V)_*(K|_{X_V})$. Restriction of $K$ is bounded constructible by intersecting its strata with $X_V$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Choose a finite affine cover $V_1,\ldots,V_t$ of $Y$. Bounds on these opens give a global bound by taking their minimum and maximum. Constructibility glues: replace each finite stratification on $V_j$ by its intersections with $V_j\setminus\bigcup_{h<j}V_h$. These are finitely many disjoint locally closed constructible strata of $Y$, covering $Y$, and finite local constancy on each is unchanged. Opens are constructible by step 1. Vanishing can be checked on the cover because a sheaf locally zero is zero. It therefore suffices to handle affine $Y$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: locality on Y and finite union of cohomological ranges

proof.text: Assume $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and take a finite affine cover $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ of $X$. The case $X=\varnothing$ gives $K=0$ and $Rf_*K=0$, so assume $r\geq1$. Write $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. Finitely many $k$-algebra generators of $B_i$ also generate it as an $R$-algebra. Thus $X_i\to Y$ has an affine-space/projective-closure compactification by [prop-nagata-affine-compactification], [def-nagata-affine-compactification] and [def-nagata-compactification]. For each nonempty $I$ choose $i\in I$. The intersection $X_I=\bigcap_{j\in I}X_j$ is an open subscheme of $X_i$, hence of this compactification $\overline X_i$. Its inclusion $j_I$ followed by $p_i:\overline X_i\to Y$ is $f_I$. Both $X_I$ and $\overline X_i$ are finite type over $k$: step 1 handles $X_I$, while $p_i$ is proper and hence finite type. Apply [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients] to $j_I$ and [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible] to $p_i$. Fix any prime $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k$ (and any finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$), so that $\ell$ is invertible on all schemes here, as the preamble of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] requires. Its clause (5), for arbitrary commutative $A$ on the small etale site, identifies $Rf_{I,*}(K|_{X_I})$ with $Rp_{i,*}Rj_{I,*}(K|_{X_I})$. Hence each belongs to $D^b_c(Y,A)$; choose bounds $a_I\leq b_I$. Empty intersections contribute zero. This uses the same open/projective factorization as blueprint paragraph 1, with the ambient closure of $X_i$ instead of taking a second closure of $X_I$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: factor the non-affine intersections as open immersions followed by proper morphisms

proof.text:
For $u_I:X_I\hookrightarrow X$, form the commuting double complex
$$D^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}f_{I,*}(J^q|_{X_I}),\qquad 0\leq p<r,$$
with alternating restriction differential and vertical differential induced by $J$. Its total differential is $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. By [lem-dg-etale-injective-finite-cech-rows], the augmented ordered Cech row of each $J^q$ is split exact on $X$. The additive functor $f_*$ preserves the splitting equations, and finite sums and composite direct images identify its row terms with the displayed $D^{p,q}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus each row augmentation $f_*J^q[0]\to D^{\bullet,q}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The degreewise restriction maps define a chain map $f_*J\to\operatorname{Tot}(D)$: the horizontal augmentation differential is zero and the vertical differential commutes with restriction. Apply [lem-sc-finite-strip-row-augmentation] with strip width $r$ to conclude this map is a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ represents $Rf_*K$. All diagonal sums are finite. If $J^q=0$ for $q<m$, reindex $q=t+m$ with $t\geq0$ in the first-quadrant total definition and put $\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\operatorname{Tot}(D^{p,t+m})^{n-m}$, with the displayed differential.

source.place: Paragraph 2: finite alternating Cech resolution after direct image and its total augmentation

proof.text:
Filter $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ by $F^p\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\bigoplus_{s\geq p}D^{s,n-s}$. This is a filtration by subcomplexes with $F^0=\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ and $F^r=0$. The graded piece is the column in horizontal degree $p$, placed in total degrees $p+q$, with differential $(-1)^p d_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. The maps required by [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core],
$$F^p/F^{p+t}\longrightarrow F^{p-t+1}/F^{p+1}\quad(t\geq1),$$
are induced by inclusions, since $F^{p+t}\subseteq F^{p+1}$. That theorem gives stabilization and a finite filtration of the abutment, with
$$E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}\mathcal H^q(Rf_{I,*}(K|_{X_I}))\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K).$$
The column formula uses step 2: each $J|_{X_I}$ is a bounded-below injective representative, and finite sums commute with kernels and images; the sign $(-1)^p$ is a unit and changes neither. The uniform horizontal filtration is finite even when $J$ is unbounded above, so no unbounded-Cech convergence assertion is needed.

source.place: Paragraphs 2–3: the displayed Cech spectral sequence and its finite abutment filtration

proof.text: Set $a=\min_I a_I$ and $b=\max_I b_I$. The first page vanishes outside $0\leq p<r$, $a\leq q\leq b$. The same is true on all later pages, each being the cohomology of the preceding page. By [thm-constructible-serre], a finite sum of constructible sheaves is constructible, by its split short exact sequences. Kernels, images (kernels of cokernels), and their quotients are constructible by the same statement. Thus every page and every stationary term is constructible. The finite filtration of $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$ supplied in step 6 has these stationary terms as its graded pieces. Induction over the finite filtration, using extension closure, proves constructibility of the abutment. For $n<a$ or $n>b+r-1$ every graded piece is zero, so the abutment is zero. This is bounded constructibility [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Step 3 glues the conclusion on $Y$. For $r=1$ there is one column; empty intersections and the zero complex give zero columns, so these cases cause no exception.

source.place: Paragraph 3: bounded rectangle, Serre closure, and finite filtration of the abutment

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between finite-type schemes over
a field $k$, and let $A$ be a finite ring annihilated by an
integer invertible in $k$. Then

$$
Rf_*:D^b_c(X,A)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,A)
$$

is defined on the ordinary derived categories. The morphism
$f$ need not be separated.

proof.text:
The assertion is local on $Y$. Choose a finite affine cover
of $Y$, prove it on each member, and take the finite union of
the resulting cohomological ranges. We may therefore assume
$Y$ affine. Cover $X$ by finitely many affine opens
$X_1,\ldots,X_r$. For each nonempty subset
$I\subset\{1,\ldots,r\}$, the intersection
$X_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}X_i$ is a quasi-compact open of the affine
scheme $X_i$ for any $i\in I$. It need not be affine.
The finite-type morphism $X_i\to Y$ admits a closed embedding
in $\mathbf A^m_Y$; hence $X_I$ is locally closed in
$\mathbf P^m_Y$. In its scheme-theoretic closure
$\overline X_I$, it is open and dense. We obtain a factorization

$$
f_I:X_I\xrightarrow{j_I}\overline X_I
\xrightarrow{p_I}Y
$$

with $j_I$ open and $p_I$ projective. The two preceding
results [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients], [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible]
prove bounded constructibility of
$Rf_{I,*}K|_{X_I}=Rp_{I,*}Rj_{I,*}K|_{X_I}$.
Composition of the derived direct images is
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] (item (5)); on cohomology
sheaves it is
[lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-spectral-sequence].

For completeness, use the finite alternating Cech resolution
of the open cover. In degree $p$ it has the direct sum over
strictly increasing index sets $i_0<\cdots<i_p$, so
$0\leq p\leq r-1$. Its augmented rows are exact: near any
point of $X$, choose a member of the cover containing that
point and contract the augmented alternating complex by inserting
its index. Apply this to an injective resolution of $K$.
Restriction to an open preserves injectives because its left
adjoint, extension by zero in
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], is exact. Thus after
applying $f_*$ the double complex gives

$$
E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}
\mathcal H^q(Rf_{I,*}K|_{X_I})
\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K).
$$

There are only finitely many subsets $I$, and each corresponding
direct image has a finite range already proved above. Hence this
spectral sequence lies in a bounded rectangle. Every term on
every page is constructible by kernels and cokernels, and each
abutment has a finite constructible filtration, using
[thm-constructible-serre]. Outside the finite sum
of the two ranges the abutment vanishes. This proves the theorem
without an unbounded Cech argument, an affine-intersection
assumption, or a closed-base-change identification for $Rj_*$.
